# File operations

Deleting, renaming, copying and linking files by name.

<h2 id="delete-file"><code>DeleteFile</code></h2>

```rux
pub func DeleteFile(allocator: Allocator, path: Path) -> ! IoError
```

Deletes the file `path` names. Removing the name does not disturb any handle still open on the file.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/FileSystem/Src/Directory.rux#L71)

**Parameters**

| Name        | Type        | Description                  |
| ----------- | ----------- | ---------------------------- |
| `allocator` | `Allocator` | where the storage comes from |
| `path`      | `Path`      | the path to act on           |

**Returns**: success when the file is gone

<h2 id="rename"><code>Rename</code></h2>

```rux
pub func Rename(allocator: Allocator, from: Path, to: Path) -> ! IoError
```

Renames `from` to `to`, moving it between directories if the paths differ there.
An existing `to` is replaced, atomically within one volume: a reader sees the old file or the new, never a
gap. Across volumes Windows copies and deletes instead — not atomic — and the Unix systems refuse.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/FileSystem/Src/Transfer.rux#L30)

**Parameters**

| Name        | Type        | Description                        |
| ----------- | ----------- | ---------------------------------- |
| `allocator` | `Allocator` | where the storage comes from       |
| `from`      | `Path`      | the path that exists now           |
| `to`        | `Path`      | the path it should have afterwards |

**Returns**: success when the file is at its new path

<h2 id="create-hard-link"><code>CreateHardLink</code></h2>

```rux
pub func CreateHardLink(allocator: Allocator, existing: Path, link: Path) -> ! IoError
```

Creates `link` as a hard link: a second name for the file `existing` names.
The two names are then equals — neither is "the original" — and the content lives until the last name is
deleted. A symbolic link at `existing` is not followed: the link is made to the name given. Directories
cannot be hard-linked on any supported system.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/FileSystem/Src/Transfer.rux#L57)

**Parameters**

| Name        | Type        | Description                  |
| ----------- | ----------- | ---------------------------- |
| `allocator` | `Allocator` | where the storage comes from |
| `existing`  | `Path`      | the file that exists now     |
| `link`      | `Path`      | the link to create           |

**Returns**: success when the new name refers to the same file

<h2 id="create-symbolic-link"><code>CreateSymbolicLink</code></h2>

```rux
pub func CreateSymbolicLink(allocator: Allocator, target: Path, link: Path, targetIsDirectory: bool) -> ! IoError
```

Creates `link` as a symbolic link holding `target` as its text.
The target is stored, not checked: a dangling link is created as readily as a good one. `targetIsDirectory`
matters only on Windows, which types its links; the Unix systems ignore it. Windows also gates creation
behind a privilege unless the machine runs Developer Mode, so `PermissionDenied` here is an environment, not
a bug.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/FileSystem/Src/Transfer.rux#L86)

**Parameters**

| Name                | Type        | Description                                                              |
| ------------------- | ----------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `allocator`         | `Allocator` | where the storage comes from                                             |
| `target`            | `Path`      | the path the link will point at, which need not exist                    |
| `link`              | `Path`      | the link to create                                                       |
| `targetIsDirectory` | `bool`      | whether the target is a directory, which Windows must be told in advance |

**Returns**: success when the link was created; Windows needs a privilege for this

<h2 id="copy-file"><code>CopyFile</code></h2>

```rux
pub func CopyFile(allocator: Allocator, from: Path, to: Path) -> ! IoError
```

Copies the file `from` names to `to`, following a symbolic link to the bytes it points at.
An existing `to` is replaced. The copy is the bytes and nothing else: permissions, timestamps and the rest of
the metadata are the destination's own, fresh — carrying them is a policy the metadata work owns.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/FileSystem/Src/Transfer.rux#L116)

**Parameters**

| Name        | Type        | Description                        |
| ----------- | ----------- | ---------------------------------- |
| `allocator` | `Allocator` | where the storage comes from       |
| `from`      | `Path`      | the path that exists now           |
| `to`        | `Path`      | the path it should have afterwards |

**Returns**: success when the destination holds a copy
